[Lähde: The Guardian World | URL: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/02/man-arrested-scottish-woman-dead-suitcase-athens]
Greek police say 26-year-old Afghan national is believed to have left Elisabeth-Jane Ross’s body in derelict building

Greek authorities have arrested an Afghan national in connection with the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in central Athens.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, a charity worker described as an “angel full of innocence and goodness” by friends, had been in Greece for almost three weeks when she is believed to have died.

Police sources said the suspect was a 26-year-old Afghan citizen who had allegedly confessed to the crime. He had been brought in for questioning by Greece’s homicide division last Thursday, two days after Ross’s body was publicly identified.

A statement released by police on Sunday said: “A criminal file has been opened against a 26-year-old foreign national for intentional homicide, robbery and violation of the law [regarding] weapons.”

Explaining the accusation of ownership of illegal weapons, security officials said “various arms – some real, some fake” had been discovered in the suspect’s home, also thought to be in the downtown area of Kypseli where the body was discovered.
 He is expected to be charged on Monday.

Throughout the investigation, Greek authorities had worked closely with the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) and Police Scotland, according to the statement.

Ross, who had strong links with the charity sector in Greece, is the daughter of a prominent lawyer in Edinburgh, where she also lived.

She was reported to have friends in Kypseli, where her body was discovered on 18 July by a homeless man in what had once been a car park. Wrapped in cloth, it had been placed in a suitcase left in a decrepit, rubbish-strewn building at the site.

Sources told the Guardian that the suspect’s alleged use of credit cards that belonged to Ross had contributed to police identifying him.

“He was caught on camera withdrawing money with the cards from various ATMs,” one said. “The credit cards belonged to Ms Ross. That played a big role in leading us to him.”

For days, investigators were unable to make headway, citing the lack of fingerprints or DNA on the suitcase. Adding to the mystery was the discovery that her mobile phone had been used until the time when the body was publicly identified last week.

Police had described text messages sent to her father and other members of her family as deliberately misleading. The messages had spoken of her “need to be alone”.

[Lähde: The Mirror | URL: https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/man-arrested-major-update-after-37505723]
A man has been arrested following the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found inside a suitcase in Athens.

The body of Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, from the Edinburgh area, was discovered by a homeless man in a derelict building in the Kypseli area of Athens on July 18. She is believed to have died between five and seven days before she was found.

And now a 26-year-old man, who Greek police said was a foreigner, has been arrested.

During the period from when she is thought to have died until Ms Ross' body was found, someone was reportedly using her mobile phone to send messages purporting to be from her.

Hellenic Police, Greece’s national force, have said they were able to identify the victim using fingerprints. Earlier this week, toxicology tests were being carried out to establish if "foul play" was involved in her death and a cause of death has not yet been given.

Ms Ross entered Greece on June 26 and was initially staying with friends in Piraeus. She is then said to have gone to meet with American friends in another part of the Greek capital, but it is unclear if this ever happened.

The Hellenic Police said they analysed video footage to identify the suspect, who confessed on Thursday. The 26-year-old man is believed to have put her body into a suitcase, taking it to the abandoned site where it was found.

In the following days he is said to have used her bank card to withdraw money. A replica pistol and a knife were found at the suspect’s home and police have filed a case against him for manslaughter, robbery and violation of weapons laws.

Previously a spokesperson for the Greek police, Konstantina Dimoglidou, said: "Our priority is to get to the bottom of who left the suitcase. Whoever they were was careful not to leave fingerprints or DNA.

"We've had the entire homicide division of the Greek FBI working on the case. We're in contact with other police forces. We're going to solve this."

The Foreign and Commonwealth Office said earlier: “Our thoughts are with Elisabeth’s family during this difficult time. We are providing consular support and are in contact with the local authorities.”

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “We are aware of the death of a Scottish woman in Athens and are liaising with authorities in Greece. Officers are providing support to her family in Scotland.”
